turns.t: Hi doctor. Sorry, I know it's silly, but I can't stop sneezing and I'm starting to panic a bit.
Not silly at all. Tell me about the sneezing. ~
It comes in fits. Like, I'll sneeze eight or nine times in a row, and then my eyes stream and my nose runs like a tap.
How long has this been going on?
Since the start of September. So about three weeks, I think. Maybe more.
Does it come at any particular time of day, or in particular places?
Mornings, mostly, and when I'm outside walking the dog. It's much better when I'm indoors with the windows shut.
That's helpful, that's a clear pattern. ~
My mate reckons it's hay fever, but I've never had it before, I'm twenty-nine, so I don't know. ~
People can develop it later, it's not unusual. Let me have a look up your nose. Tilt your head back. ~
Okay. Is this going to hurt? ~
Not at all, it's just a light. Keep still.
Is everything all right in there? ~
The lining of your nose is pale and a bit swollen on both sides. Nothing blocking it.
Is that bad? ~
No, it's what I'd expect with a lot of sneezing, and there's nothing sinister. ~
I just wanted to make sure it wasn't something serious, like a growth or something. ~
Nothing here suggests that at all. Try not to google it at midnight. ~
Too late, I did. ~
Everyone does. What sort of dog have you got, by the way? ~
A spaniel called Biscuit. She's a nightmare in the long grass, she comes back covered in seeds. ~
Spaniels are brilliant at collecting whatever's floating about outside, so that fits with your pattern. ~
She does love a hedge. ~
Right. Well, to find out what is triggering it, I'd like to arrange a skin prick test.
What happens in that? ~
We put tiny drops of common triggers like pollen and dust on your forearm and prick the skin lightly. A few spots go red and itchy, and that tells us what you react to. ~
That doesn't sound too bad. When? ~
The nurse will book you in, within a fortnight or so. Don't take any antihistamines for three days beforehand, or the test won't work.
Okay. And meanwhile? ~
Keep the windows shut in the morning, shower and change when you get in from the dog walk, and wash the dog's bed.
That I can do. Will it go away? ~
Most people get it under control once we know the trigger. I'd like to see you again in three weeks to go over the test.
Three weeks. Great. Thanks, doctor, I feel calmer now. ~
Good. Go and enjoy the dog. ~

symptoms.name: fits
symptoms.normalized_name: Sneezing fits with watery eyes and runny nose
